original_question: Can the direct finite-temperature loop expansion of the functional renormalization group be reorganized or resummed in a consistent way, equivalent to the exact renormalization-group treatment, so that it remains quantitatively valid beyond the low-loop regime instead of failing in the thermal boundary layer?
target_in_paper: An outstanding question in the functional RG is how temperature regularizes the otherwise singular flow of the zero-temperature FRG, mapping to the viscous‐layer regularization of inertial range Burgers turbulence (i.e. to the construction of the inviscid limit).
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies that the direct finite-temperature loop expansion of the FRG fails in the thermal boundary layer and asks whether it can be reorganized or resummed in a way equivalent to the exact (ERG) treatment so as to remain valid beyond low-loop orders.
missing_details: Specify the physical system: pinned elastic manifolds of internal dimension d under quenched disorder
Define the FRG quantity: the renormalized disorder correlator function R(u)
Precisely describe the thermal boundary layer regime: u∼O(T) and its role in the failure of the loop expansion
State that the failure is demonstrated already for d=0 (Sinai model) requiring the ERG hierarchy
Mention the loop orders at which perturbation fails (one- and two-loop in ε=4−d expansion)
Clarify that the ERG refers to the nonperturbative functional hierarchy of flow equations for cumulants
Quantify the goal: reproduce exact R(u) at arbitrary temperature T and internal dimension d
refined_question: In the context of the functional renormalization group applied to pinned elastic manifolds of internal dimension d at finite temperature T>0, the direct perturbative loop expansion for the renormalized disorder correlator R(u) breaks down in the thermal boundary layer regime (u∼O(T)), as demonstrated by its failure already in the d=0 Sinai model and the ensuing requirement for a nonperturbative ERG functional hierarchy. Is there a systematic reorganization or resummation of this finite-temperature loop expansion that reproduces the exact ERG results for R(u) and remains quantitatively valid beyond one- and two-loop orders for arbitrary d and T?
justification: The target open question appears explicitly in the introduction as the ‘outstanding question’ of how temperature regularizes the singular T=0 FRG flow by analogy to viscous-layer regularization in Burgers turbulence, motivating the development of the ERG hierarchy when the loop expansion fails in the thermal boundary layer ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/author/7003957225/pierre-l-le-doussal?utm_source=openai)). The draft captures the gist of this question but omits crucial details about the system (pinned elastic manifolds), the object R(u), the specific regime (u∼O(T)), the counterexample at d=0, and the failure at low-loop orders, which are all essential for a stand-alone, paper-faithful statement ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.1192)).
